whatThisIs: The questionnaire capture form, declared ONCE. Every client and every guide that claims to
describe this form is measured against this file, and never against each other.
THE OWNER'S REPORT, VERBATIM: "all the fields on the questionnaire page that are there on the
web application, should be exactly there on the android app as well, the checkbox list should be
replaced with multi-select dropdown for artisans over there as well, web implementation is
correct, I want the same thing for android as well, create contracts so that the two do not
drift". This file is the last clause. The `fields` list below is the first three.
whyAContractAndNotAParityTest: A test that compares the web form against the Android form answers the wrong question twice.
It cannot say WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT. `test_walkthrough_fields_parity.py` in the sibling designer
portal is the two-way form, and it is honest about the cost: its failure message has to end
"The web is the register: fix steps.ts and WALKTHROUGH_FIELDS together" because the assertion
itself cannot tell you that. A reader who does not already know the rule can make it green from
either end, and the quickest end is usually the wrong one.
AND IT GOES GREEN WHEN BOTH SIDES DRIFT THE SAME WAY. That was not a hypothetical here. Both
walkthrough registers in this repository — `frontend/components/guide/steps.ts` and
`android/.../ui/WalkthroughSteps.kt` — named a "Date" field that the form had not had for as long
as the comment at page.tsx:997 had been there, and both omitted Workshop, Questionnaire, Status
and Interview notes. `WalkthroughStepsTest.kt` held those two registers EQUAL to each other and
PASSED, because they were equally wrong. Two copies agreeing is not evidence; it is the failure
mode.
Both were regenerated on 2026-09-16 and are green against this file. The paragraph stays in the
past tense rather than going, because it is the only account of WHY this file is shaped the way
it is — and because the green suite it describes is still green and still cannot see the thing it
missed. A reader who arrives after the registers are correct would otherwise find a two-way test
passing, this file apparently redundant, and no record that the two facts once coexisted.
So this file names the intended truth once and every surface is joined to IT. The register-to-
register edge already exists in WalkthroughStepsTest.kt and is deliberately not repeated by the
enforcing test — what was missing is the edge from each register to the form, which is the only
edge that can notice a claim both registers make and neither screen honours.
THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, and why it is not enough: generate the Android form from this file at
build time, so drift is impossible rather than merely detected. It would work, and it is the
right shape for a product whose two clients draw the same widgets — which these do not. A
Compose column and a CSS grid disagree about what "order" even means at a breakpoint, the web's
status control is a `<Select>` or a locked chip by role, and the handset's is a dropdown or a
chip by the same role through different primitives. A generator would have to model both widget
sets to emit either, and the first control that did not fit would be written by hand beside it,
unguarded, which is where this started. Declaring the truth and checking both readings of it
leaves each client free to draw it natively and still refuses to let them mean different things.
howOrderIsPartOfIt: The `fields` array is in WEB SCREEN ORDER and that order is contractual, not incidental.
A form whose boxes appear in one sequence on a laptop and another on a handset is a form a
researcher has to re-learn on each device, and they re-learn it in a courtyard with an artisan
waiting. It is also the thing a printed guide gets wrong most usefully: `docs/WALKTHROUGH.md`
gets read with the form open beside it, so a list in the wrong sequence sends the reader
hunting for a box two fields further down and, finding the wrong one, filling it in.
THE TWO CLIENTS DISAGREED ABOUT THIS AND THE WEB WON. The web draws the three text boxes first
and then the workshop (page.tsx:989-1031, "The workshop leads every other dropdown"); the handset
opened with the workshop. Both orders are defensible in isolation, and exactly one of them can be
the contract. The owner ruled the web correct, so the handset's field block was re-ordered to
match (MainActivity.kt:12771-13216, where the argument is written out at the head of the block).
This paragraph was written while the disagreement was still live and said so in the present
tense. It is kept in the past tense rather than deleted, because the ORDER is the half of this
contract with no other evidence behind it: a reader who finds `fields` in an order that is not
alphabetical, not the database's and not the API's needs to know it is the web's screen order and

why: THE CONTROL VOCABULARY, declared once: which component on each client draws which kind
of control, and how that component says its own label.
IT LIVES HERE AND NOT ON THE FIELDS because how a control labels itself is a property of
the CONTROL, not of the field it happens to be drawing. `MultiNoteInput` defaults its
label to "Notes" for every caller in the application, not only for this form, and a
copy of that fact on each field would be a register with as many copies as there are
fields using it.
IT IS ALSO WHAT KEEPS THE CONTRACT FROM CONTRADICTING ITSELF. A field names a `control`
kind AND the component each client draws it with; the enforcing test checks that the
named component is registered under the named kind. Without that join a field could
declare `"control": "text"` and `"composable": "DropdownField"` in the same breath —
which the first draft of this file did for `language`, and nothing would have caught it:
the handset would have been held to a dropdown by a contract that said free text.
THE SCANNER READS THIS WHOLE LIST rather than only the components each field names, so a
field drawn with the WRONG registered control is reported as the swap it is ('drawn with
DropdownField, contract declares TextInput') instead of as a field that is missing. The
`checkbox-wall` kind exists for exactly that reason and for no other: no field may
declare it — see `controlPins.forbidden` — but the scanner has to be able to FIND one to
say that it is there.

fields.label: Interview title
fields.note: What this sitting is called in every list that shows it; title-cased by the server on save.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: Where the interview happened; title-cased by the server, like the title and unlike the language.

fields.label: Language
note: The language the interview was conducted in, as FREE TEXT and not a closed vocabulary.
The web argues this where it draws it (page.tsx:1012-1018): the column is `str | None` with no
enum behind it on either side, and the artisan's own answer — "Kutchi, and some Gujarati" — is
a perfectly good value that no list of language names can hold. A dropdown here is not a
narrower version of this control; it is a different control that cannot express the answer.
THE HANDSET DREW A DROPDOWN — twenty-four scheduled languages plus "Other", preserving any
pre-existing free-text value as an extra option — AND THE OWNER'S RULING MADE THAT A DRIFT. It
was not in the reported list, which named the missing fields and the artisan widget; it is
recorded here because a contract that quietly omitted it would be the third register in this
repository that looks authoritative and is held to nothing.
CLOSED on 2026-09-16: the handset now draws `TextInput("Language", …)` (MainActivity.kt:12795)
and the "Other" row is gone with the list. The "Other" row is worth one more sentence, because
it is the proof rather than a detail — it recorded that the researcher had an answer and then
threw the answer away. The dropdown's `?: "Hindi"` seed went with it: on a closed vocabulary a
default is a starting position, on a free-text box it is an ANSWER the form supplies on the
researcher's behalf, indistinguishable in the archive from one they typed.

fields.label: Workshop
note: The workshop this interview belongs to — the context that scopes the artisan roster offered
below it and the interviews the browse screens list.
Neither client writes this label at the call site: the web's `WorkshopSelect` defaults
`label = "Workshop"` (WorkshopSelect.tsx:406) and the handset's `WorkshopField` reaches
`WorkshopDropdown`, which defaults the same string (MainActivity.kt:4119). That is why the
enforcing test resolves a `componentDefault` label out of the component's own file instead of
scanning the form for a literal — a scan for literals alone reports this field as missing from
both clients, which is the parser lying rather than the form drifting.

fields.label: Questionnaire
note: WHICH INSTRUMENT this sitting is answering — the questionnaire whose sections and questions the
rest of the screen then draws.
ABSENT FROM THE HANDSET ENTIRELY as of this contract's first version: `questionnaireId` does not
occur once in MainActivity.kt (it exists only in the data layer, ApiModels/FieldRepository/
FieldRepositoryApi), so the handset answers whichever instrument its `sections` were loaded
from and the researcher is never asked. On a deployment with one instrument that is invisible;
on the third workshop with a revised instrument beside the original it is an interview filed
against the wrong questionnaire with nothing on the screen that could have said so.
It sits immediately after the workshop on the web because the workshop is usually what chooses
it — page.tsx:1027-1033 also records why it is a `<Field>` + `<Select>` and not a `<details>`:
the capture e2e spec locates this form's sections as `form.panel details`, so a collapsible
control here joins that set and breaks the spec while reading as a styling change.

fields.label: Status
note: The record's review state. A control kind of its own rather than a `select`, because on both
clients it is TWO controls chosen by role and a contract that called it a dropdown would be
describing only the half that admins see.
Web (page.tsx:1054-1074): a `<Select>` of DRAFT/PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED defaulting to
APPROVED when `canPickStatus`, otherwise a locked "Pending" chip carrying the sentence "New
interviews are submitted for review as Pending." Handset (MainActivity.kt:3696): `StatusControl`
makes the same split on `canSetStatus`, `StatusDropdown` above it and a Pending chip below.
Both label the whole control "Status", in both arms — which is what the enforcing test reads.

fields.label: Artisans interviewed
note: Everybody this interview is with. ONE control for the whole set, searchable, never a wall of
checkboxes — see `controlPins` below, which is where that is made structural rather than a
matter of what this note says.
The web reached one control by an earlier round of the same complaint (page.tsx:1075-1092): it
used to draw "Primary" and "Additional" artisans as two dropdowns, the database join has no
rank column, and the form already de-duplicated the two into one set before every request it
sent — so the split only ever created work, and a set assembled two ways could leave the RESP
block describing nobody.
THE FOUR-SENTENCE EMPTY MESSAGE IS PART OF THIS FIELD AND MUST SURVIVE ANY WIDGET SWAP. An empty
roster means one of four different things — the request is in flight, the request failed,
nobody is recorded at this workshop, nobody is recorded at all — and only two of them are facts
about the repository. Printing "No artisans are recorded at this workshop yet" off an empty
array while the answer is still coming makes a claim before it exists, and the researcher who
believes it goes off to create a duplicate of an artisan who is already there. Both clients
print the same four sentences off the same three facts today (page.tsx `emptyLabel`,
MainActivity.kt `emptyMessage`), and the argument for them is written out at both call sites
and in `ArtisanMultiSelectField`'s own KDoc. Whoever moves this field onto
`SearchableMultiSelectField` carries those four sentences and that reasoning across; the
widget is what changes, not what the form is able to say.

fields.label: Interview notes
note: Free notes about the sitting, as a repeating group: one textarea per note with an "Add note"
button and a per-note remove, joined on a blank line into the single `notes` column.
PRESENT ON BOTH CLIENTS AND ONCE LABELLED DIFFERENTLY, which was the quietest of the drifts
here. The web writes the label at the call site (`<MultiNoteField name="notes"
label="Interview notes" />`, page.tsx:1447); the handset called `MultiNoteInput(value = notes,
dictate = false)` with no label at all and took that composable's default, which is "Notes"
(MainActivity.kt:15428). Nothing was missing, nothing was broken, and the two screens called one
box two names — which is exactly the class of difference a reader dismisses as cosmetic until
they are trying to explain a form over a phone line, and exactly why it outlived two releases
that both claimed parity.
CLOSED on 2026-09-16 by writing the label at the handset's call site (MainActivity.kt:13216).
THE COMPOSABLE'S DEFAULT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: changing `label: String = "Notes"` would
rename the notes box on every other record form in the application to fix one screen, and four
forms that say "Notes" about notes are not wrong. That is also what makes this contract's
`labelFrom: composableDefault` rule load-bearing rather than decorative — the enforcing test has
to read the default to know that a call site which stops passing a label has silently renamed
the box back.

why: THE OWNER ASKED FOR THIS ONE BY NAME: "the checkbox list should be replaced with multi-select
dropdown for artisans over there as well".
PINNED BY THE CONTROL AND NOT BY THE LABEL, because a label check cannot see this defect. The
handset drew `ArtisanMultiSelectField` (declared at MainActivity.kt:4358), which paints a Column
of checkboxes — every artisan at the workshop, one row each, straight into the form — under a
"(n selected)" caption. Rename that control's label to the contract's word and every assertion
about labels goes green over a wall of checkboxes that is still a wall of checkboxes. So the
enforcing test asserts WHICH COMPOSABLE DRAWS THE FIELD, and `forbidden` names the two that must
not: a future edit that swaps the widget back is caught as the widget change it is.
ONLY ONE OF THE TWO FORBIDDEN NAMES STILL PAINTS CHECKBOXES, and the second is listed for a
different reason that has to be said or the failure message misleads. `CheckboxMultiSelectField`
(MainActivity.kt:4479) is TODAY a four-line alias that forwards straight to
`SearchableMultiSelectField` — it was rewritten onto it and kept its old name, so drawing this
field with it would in fact produce the control the owner asked for, under a name that says the
opposite. It stays forbidden HERE anyway: this contract's job is to be readable by somebody
checking the handset against the browser, and a line reading
`CheckboxMultiSelectField(label = "Artisans interviewed")` reads as the defect whatever it
compiles to. It is also one rename away from being true again — a name nobody has to honour is
a name somebody eventually re-implements.
THE REGISTRY ENTRY IS LEFT AT `checkbox-wall` RATHER THAN CORRECTED TO WHAT IT DRAWS. That kind
is a sentinel in `controls` — see its `why`: it exists so the scanner can FIND a control no
field may declare, not to describe pixels — and moving this entry to `searchable-multiselect`
would make the control-kind assertion pass on a line the `forbidden` assertion still rejects,
which is two checks disagreeing about one call site. The rejected alternative was to drop
`CheckboxMultiSelectField` from `forbidden` altogether now that it is harmless; that trades a
misleading failure message for no failure at all, and the message is the cheaper thing to fix.
CLOSED on 2026-09-16 — the capture form draws `SearchableMultiSelectField` at
MainActivity.kt:12896, and the browse screen's filter (see `distinctLabels`) was swapped in the
same pass, because the owner's complaint was about the widget and not about one screen.
`ArtisanMultiSelectField` still EXISTS and still has one caller — the Workshop record form's own
"Linked artisans" box, which the web also calls "Linked artisans" (workshops/page.tsx:630), so
that surviving label is web parity rather than the residue of this drift. `forbidden` therefore
names a composable that is still in the file on purpose: this pin is about which control draws
THIS field, not about deleting a control from the application.
`SearchableMultiSelectField` already exists in this repository
(android/.../ui/SearchableSelect.kt:304) and is what `CheckboxMultiSelectField` was itself
rewritten onto — a summary trigger, the chosen rows as chips, and a searchable sheet with
"Select all". Its own KDoc gives the argument against the wall it replaced: the wall has no
summary line, so the only way to see what is ticked is to scroll the form back over it, and no
room for a Select-all row without pushing the next field further down a page that is already
long. There is no third control to write, and writing one would be the whole problem again.
The web is already there: `MultiSelectDropdown` (components/ui/Dropdown.tsx) is a thin adapter
over `SearchableMultiSelect`, and the questionnaire page forces `searchable` on rather than
leaving it to an option count — one workshop on this deployment, forty on the next, and a
control that changes shape between two workshops for reasons the researcher cannot see.
THERE IS NO DATE CONTROL ON THIS FORM, ON EITHER CLIENT, AND THAT IS A DECISION.
The server derives `interviewDate` from `recordedAt`, which is when the interview was actually
captured. page.tsx:997 records the reasoning where the box used to be — asking a researcher to
confirm today's date was a field to tab past that could only ever be wrong — and adds the
second half, that a spoken date is the one thing a recogniser gets wrong in a way that still
parses, so no microphone would go on one even if it came back. `frontend/components/forms/
RecordedAtField.tsx` is a deprecated stub that renders null for the same reason, across every
record form. The handset says the same thing in the comment at MainActivity.kt:12772-12776.
IT IS IN THIS CONTRACT AS A NEGATIVE BECAUSE ALL THREE GUIDES STILL CLAIM IT. steps.ts,
WalkthroughSteps.kt and docs/WALKTHROUGH.md each list "Date" between the title and the place.
A guide naming a field that was removed on purpose sends the reader looking for it, and a
printed guide does it to somebody with no signal to check against. A contract that only ever
said what SHOULD be there could not catch this: the registers are supersets of the field list
by design, so an extra entry is invisible to a floor check. This is the ceiling.
The labelled controls each form draws that are NOT fields of this contract, declared per client
with a reason, so that the enforcing test can compare an EQUALITY instead of a containment.
Without this list the only assertion available is "every contract field appears somewhere",
which is silent about a NEW box appearing on one client and not the other — the drift that
started this, running in the other direction. With it, any labelled control on either form that
is neither a contract field nor a line below fails, and the person who added it has to say which
it is. That is the whole cost of the list and it is meant to be paid at the moment a control is
added rather than at the next desync.

android.label: Recording mode
why: How answers are captured — per question, or one take for a whole section. The web asks the
same question through `QuestionnaireCaptureControls` (page.tsx:1264), a component that lives
outside this form file and whose labels are therefore invisible to a scan of the form region.
It is a capture PREFERENCE and not a property of the interview: nothing it sets is stored on
the record, which is why it is not a field of this contract on either client.

android.label: Answer
why: The typed answer to ONE question, drawn once per question inside the sections loop. Its web
counterpart is a bare `<TextArea>` labelled by `aria-labelledby` against the question prompt
rather than by a `label=` literal, so the two clients genuinely do differ in how this box is
named — and it is the question prompt, not a form label, that names it on both.
It belongs to the instrument rather than to this form: there are as many of these as the
questionnaire has questions, they are keyed by question id, and no fixed register could list
them. All three guides describe them in the one line they can — "Per question: ..." — which
is licensed under `paraphrases` below.

distinctLabels.label: Involved artisan(s)
why: THE BROWSE SCREEN'S ARTISAN FILTER KEEPS ITS OWN WORD, DELIBERATELY. It is a different control
on a different screen doing a different job: it narrows a list of interviews that already
exist, and ticking somebody there asserts nothing about any record.
The capture form's label is a claim about the interview being written — these are the artisans
this interview is with. "Artisans interviewed" on a filter row would read as a claim of the
same kind about rows the researcher is merely looking through, and the two screens would then
use one phrase for a statement and for a query.
THE WEB AGREES BY PRECEDENT RATHER THAN BY COINCIDENCE: the web has no control called
"Artisans interviewed" anywhere outside this form, and its own browse filter
(components/FunnelFilters.tsx:153) names itself "Filter by artisan" — filter wording for a
filter, exactly as here.
THE ALTERNATIVE, REJECTED: make every artisan control in the product say one thing, on the
argument that one control should have one name. That argument is right and it is about ONE
control; these are two. Unifying them would mean either the filter claiming to interview
people or the capture form describing its subject as a filter term, and the second is how
"Linked artisans" got onto the capture form in the first place.
IT IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE, RATHER THAN LEFT UNSAID, so that the enforcing test can hold it: the
site must still exist and must still use this word. A licence nobody checks is the third
register again — it would read as a considered decision long after the screen it describes had
been renamed or deleted.
The three places that DESCRIBE this form to a researcher. Each is joined to the field list
above, and none of them is joined to another — the register-to-register edge already exists in
`android/app/src/test/java/com/fieldrepository/app/ui/WalkthroughStepsTest.kt`, which holds
`walkthroughJourney` equal to `steps.ts` field for field, and which passes today over two
registers that are equally wrong about the form.
A FLOOR AND A CEILING, NOT AN EQUALITY. Every field in this contract must be NAMED in each
register; a register may name MORE, because it describes a whole screen and this contract
describes the interview's own boxes — "Per question: ..." is a true thing to tell a researcher
and has no single label to be equal to. The ceiling is `absent` above: what a register may not
do is name a field the form deliberately does not have.
The sibling portal learned the floor-not-equality rule the expensive way and wrote it down:
making the check symmetric there would have reported the printed guide as wrong FOR BEING RIGHT,
and the quickest way to green would have been deleting true sentences about the one field that
stops the archive filling with duplicate artisans.

web.shape: GuideStep.fields — the real form labels, in screen order, with (required) marked

printed.heading: Questionnaire
shape: One prose sentence, markdown, hard-wrapped. Compared loosely — lowercased with punctuation
collapsed — because the guide writes "**Craft** *(required)*" for a register's "Craft
(required)" and that emphasis is typography, not a different claim about the form. The strict
character-for-character comparison is kept for the two CLIENTS, where "Do's" against "Do's"
really is one screen calling one box two names.
This is the copy that gets printed and carried into a village with no signal, which is why it
is held at all: it is the only rendering whose reader cannot check it against the screen.

why: THE ESCAPE HATCH, AND IT IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. A row here says: this register is allowed to name
this field with THIS wording instead of the contract's label, for the reason the row gives.
Empty today because no register needs one. Every contract field is a short noun phrase that all
three guides can print as written, and the four fields the registers currently fail to name
(Workshop, Questionnaire, Status, Interview notes) fail by being absent, not by being said
differently — a paraphrase row for any of them would be licensing a sentence nobody has written.
THE MECHANISM SHIPS ANYWAY, because the day a register genuinely needs one is the day somebody
would otherwise weaken the floor check to get past it. The printed guide already says one true
thing a label list cannot — "then per question either a **\"Record this question\"** audio clip
or a typed answer" — and prose has a grammar for a repeating block that a chip does not.
EVERY ROW IS ITSELF CHECKED, both ways: the wording it licenses must still be in the document
(a licence for a sentence that has been rewritten is a licence for nothing), and the field it
covers must NOT be named plainly in that register (a special case still switched on after the
guide started saying the plain thing makes this table a worse description of where the document
is allowed to be loose than no table at all). A licence is only ever a licence to say a TRUE
thing differently — the sibling portal spent a cycle licensing prose against two register
entries that were themselves wrong, which is this file's own subject one level down: a
paraphrase row makes a claim look considered.

maintenance: WHEN THE WEB FORM CHANGES, this file changes in the same commit, and then both clients and all
three registers. Not the other way round: an edit that changes a client to match a form is a fix,
an edit that changes this file to match a client is a decision, and they should not look alike in
a diff.
WHEN THE ENFORCING TEST FAILS, it names the file and the line. Read that line before editing this
file. The failure modes it cannot tell apart on its own are the two that matter — a client that
drifted, and a form that legitimately grew a field nobody has recorded here yet — and only a
person can say which, which is the point of a contract having prose in it.
WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER, each because it is already one register somewhere
else and a second copy here would be the failure this file exists to prevent:
* THE LOCATION GROUP. The web draws `<LocationFields />` (page.tsx:1276) and the handset draws
`LocationAddressEditor` (MainActivity.kt:13017); both are shared components used by every
record form, both carry their own stated-address / "Captured at" split and their own long
argument for it, and the two clients are already joined by
`backend/tests/test_android_location_compat.py`. Listing State, District, Pincode, Latitude
and the rest here would put a second copy of that register in a file about questionnaires.
* MEDIA CAPTURE. `MediaCaptureField` / `MediaCaptureSection`, same argument: one component per
client, used by every form, with its own tests.
* THE QUESTIONS THEMSELVES. They come from the instrument, which the server publishes; a
hand-kept list of them is the exact thing the instrument exists to make unnecessary.
